text: Denmark is a generally flat country with wide, open fields between towns.
Suburban areas are usually open, with space between buildings.
Urban cores are more dense and built up.

clues.title: Architecture: Red Bricks
text: Much of the architecture in Denmark consists of red brick.
Roofs often have orange, dark brown or black tiles.
Similar brick architecture is also common in the Netherlands and Belgium.

clues.title: Architecture: Timer Frame Walls
text: Some older or rural buildings have timber frame walls.
Timber framing can be found in other Western and Central European countries as well, but are an especially common wall type for historical buildings in Denmark.

clues.title: Language: Danish
text: Danish is a North Germanic language, closely related to Norwegian and Swedish. The Danish alphabet contains the special letters **Æ, Ø**, and **Å**.
NOTE:
Norwegian also uses **Æ, Ø**, and **Å**.
Faroese uses **Æ and Ø** but not **Å**.
Icelandic only uses **Æ**.
Swedish only uses **Å**. In addition, Swedish uses **Ä** and **Ö**, which are not found in Danish.
The Danish word for road is **vej**. This is unlike Swedish which uses **väg** or **vägen** and Norwegian which uses **vei**/**veien** or **veg**/**vegen** (depending on spelling).
The Danish word for street is **gade**. This is unlike Swedish which uses **gata** or **gatan** and Norwegian which uses **gate, gata** or rarely **gaten**.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
